claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state, provenance, source artifacts, checkpoints, and safe next actions across agent ecosystems.

The retrieval benchmark found parity in passed cases (17/20) while one-shot BM25 recovered 48/53 evidence items at about 1,070 mean estimated tokens and the prototype workspace recovered 46/53 at about 2,932. This establishes a regression baseline, not proof that a persistent workspace intrinsically costs more tokens: the evaluated process-per-operation shell can replay context, so cumulative cached replay and genuinely uncached input must be reported separately under the new gate.

The first persistent build slice is a typed, snapshot-pinned workspace service that can reopen a parent checkpoint at revision N, refresh to N+1 with an inspectable evidence/constraint diff, batch exact and lexical query plus source-native reads, expose a pluggable semantic retrieval path, and atomically commit an immutable child checkpoint containing its parent ID and source references without reconstructing the full prior corpus.

The slice clears the transition gate when each harness case completes in no more than four workspace calls, reproduces the claims obtained through direct-filesystem access, exposes the N-to-N+1 diff, produces an immutable child linked to its parent with preserved source lineage, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

current_state: The product thesis remains agent-first durable continuity rather than retrieval as an end product.
Evaluation is complete enough to authorize implementation; the BM25 shell and its token figures remain regression evidence, not the target architecture or proof of an inherent workspace cost.

The implementation boundary is now defined around reopening revision N, refreshing to N+1, exposing the delta, performing batched typed retrieval/read operations, and committing an immutable child checkpoint.
Canonical storage, deployment, and semantic-provider choices remain deliberately unsettled.
decisions: Use a persistent snapshot-pinned workspace instead of the process-per-operation BM25 shell prototype.
Treat BM25 as a regression fixture and separate cumulative cached replay from uncached input in all token reporting.
Require exact and lexical retrieval in the first slice, with semantic retrieval behind a pluggable interface.
Preserve parent linkage, immutable revision identity, and original source references in every committed child checkpoint.
Do not reconstruct the complete prior corpus when the parent checkpoint and revision delta provide sufficient evidence.
